hints.content:
We expand the parentheses using the **distributive property**:

$\blueD A(B+C+D)=\blueD A\cdot B+\blueD A\cdot C+\blueD A\cdot D$

We can also think about the problem using an area model:

[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: Three rectangles of different sizes make up a larger rectangle. At the left, a rectangle has the width of negative m cubed and a length of m. At the rectangle in the middle, the width is m squared and the length is m. At the rectangle on the right, it has a width of three m with a length of m.

hints.content:
Here's how the solution goes, algebraically:

$\begin{align}
&\phantom{=}\goldE{m}(-m^3+m^2+3m)
\\\\
&=\goldE{m}(-m^3)+\goldE{m}(m^2)+\goldE{m}(3m)
\\\\
&=-m^4+m^3+3m^2
\end{align}$

Here's how the solution looks in terms of the area model:

[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: Three rectangles of different sizes make up a larger rectangle. At the left, a rectangle has the width of negative m cubed and a length of m. Inside of this rectangle is negative m to the fourth power. At the rectangle in the middle, the width is m squared and the length is m. Inside of this rectangle is m cubed. At the rectangle on the right, it has a width of three m with a length of m. Inside of this rectangle is three m squared.
